BiblicalUsage: Eight times, always of cruelty in human hands. The adulterer's years go to the cruel one; the wicked man's tender mercies are cruel; a cruel messenger is sent against the rebel; and the invaders from the north are cruel, and have no mercy. The word moves from the bedroom to the battlefield, and in every place it names the same thing: power without pity.
TheologicalSignificance: Proverbs keeps putting mercy and cruelty side by side, and the contrast is the lesson. The merciful man does good to his own soul; the cruel man troubles his own flesh — I believe that is the Bible's own verdict: cruelty is not strength, it is a wound the cruel inflict on themselves.
